blocks.text: India's **industrial policy** shifted from the **licence-permit Raj** to **liberalisation (1991)** and now to **manufacturing-led initiatives** — **Make in India, PLI schemes, Start-up & Stand-up India** — aiming to raise the manufacturing share and generate jobs.

rows: Basis of the public-sector-led 'mixed economy'; three schedules of industries.
**Abolished licensing (mostly), reduced public-sector reservation, allowed FDI** — LPG.
Boost manufacturing to **25% of GDP**; 25 sectors; ease of doing business.
**Start-up India (2016)** — innovation/funding; **Stand-up India** — loans for SC/ST & women entrepreneurs.

items: PLI = production-linked incentives; Stand-up India = SC/ST & women loans.

prelimsPointers: **Industrial Policy Resolution 1956** — public-sector-led mixed economy (basis of planning-era industry).
**New Industrial Policy 1991** — **abolished industrial licensing (mostly), opened FDI, reduced PSU reservation**.
**Make in India (2014)** — raise manufacturing to **25% of GDP**.
**PLI (Production-Linked Incentive)** schemes — **14 sectors** (electronics, pharma, semiconductors, auto).
**Start-up India (2016)** — funding, tax benefits, incubation.
**Stand-up India** — bank loans (₹10 lakh-1 crore) for **SC/ST & women** entrepreneurs.
**MSMEs** are the backbone of employment; **Udyam** registration.
mainsAngles: Evaluate India's industrial policy shift and the Make-in-India initiative.

glossary.definition: The New Industrial Policy that dismantled the licence-permit Raj and opened the economy.
The 2014 initiative to boost domestic manufacturing to 25% of GDP.
Production-Linked Incentive schemes rewarding incremental manufacturing output.

sections.heading: SEZs, industrial corridors, energy & power policies

blocks.text: To drive industry, India promotes **Special Economic Zones (SEZs), industrial corridors, and energy/power reforms** — expanding infrastructure and renewable capacity to meet growing demand and climate goals.

rows: **SEZ Act (2005)** — duty-free enclaves for exports; single-window; e.g. many in AP/coast.
**Electricity Act (2003)**; unbundling; **UDAY** (discom finances); One Nation One Grid.
Target **500 GW non-fossil capacity by 2030**; solar (ISA), wind; National Solar Mission.
Coal (dominant), oil imports, **National Green Hydrogen Mission, ethanol blending**.

items: SEZ Act 2005 (export enclaves); corridors (DMIC, VCIC); Electricity Act 2003 + UDAY.
Renewables target 500 GW non-fossil by 2030; Green Hydrogen Mission.

prelimsPointers: **SEZ Act (2005)** — duty-free export enclaves; **VCIC (Visakhapatnam-Chennai)** corridor passes through AP.
Industrial corridors — **Delhi-Mumbai (DMIC), Vizag-Chennai, Chennai-Bengaluru, Amritsar-Kolkata (AKIC)**.
**Electricity Act (2003)** — unbundled generation/transmission/distribution.
**UDAY** scheme — revival of discom (distribution company) finances.
India targets **500 GW of non-fossil (renewable) capacity by 2030**.
**International Solar Alliance (ISA)** — India-France initiative (HQ Gurugram).
**National Green Hydrogen Mission** & **ethanol blending (20% by 2025-26)** for energy transition.
mainsAngles: Discuss SEZs, industrial corridors and energy policy in India's industrial strategy.

glossary.definition: A Special Economic Zone — a duty-free enclave with liberal rules to promote exports.
A planned belt of industrial nodes linked by transport infrastructure (e.g. DMIC, VCIC).
The Ujwal DISCOM Assurance Yojana to restore power-distribution companies' finances.

blocks.text: The **1991 economic reforms**, triggered by a **balance-of-payments crisis**, launched **Liberalisation, Privatisation and Globalisation (LPG)** — dismantling controls, opening to foreign capital and trade, and setting India on a high-growth path.

rows: **1991 BoP/forex crisis** (gold pledged); PM **P.V. Narasimha Rao**, FM **Manmohan Singh**.
**Abolished licensing, freed prices, reduced tariffs, deregulated interest rates**.
**FDI/FII, current-account convertibility, WTO integration, export orientation**.
**Higher growth, foreign investment, services boom**; but inequality & farm-sector concerns.

items: 1991 BoP crisis → LPG (Rao-Manmohan); liberalisation (delicensing), privatisation (disinvestment), globalisation (FDI/trade).
Rupee devalued; new industrial & trade policy 1991.

prelimsPointers: **1991 reforms** triggered by a **balance-of-payments (forex) crisis**; India pledged gold to the Bank of England.
Architects — PM **P.V. Narasimha Rao** & FM **Dr. Manmohan Singh**.
**Liberalisation** — end of the **licence-permit Raj**; delicensing; tariff cuts.
**Privatisation** — **disinvestment** of public-sector undertakings.
**Globalisation** — **FDI, FII, convertibility, WTO membership (1995)**.
The **rupee was devalued** and made convertible on the current account.
Reforms shifted India from a **controlled to a market-oriented** economy.
mainsAngles: Assess the impact of the 1991 LPG reforms on the Indian economy.

glossary.definition: The 1991 Liberalisation, Privatisation and Globalisation policy overhaul.
The sale of government equity in public-sector undertakings.
The 1991 forex shortage that forced India's economic reforms.

sections.heading: International trade, Balance of Payments & India–WTO

blocks.text: **International trade** connects India to the world economy. The **Balance of Payments (BoP)** records all external transactions, and the **WTO** governs the rules of global trade — an arena where India defends its farmers and developing-country interests.

rows: **Exports – imports**; India runs a **trade deficit** (esp. crude oil, gold).
Succeeded **GATT**; HQ **Geneva**; agreements on goods (GATT), services (GATS), IP (TRIPS), agriculture (AoA).
Defends **MSP/public stockholding (peace clause), farmer subsidies**; opposes rich-country farm subsidies.

items: BoP = current + capital account; India runs a trade deficit (oil & gold imports).
WTO (1995) agreements: GATT/GATS/TRIPS/AoA; India defends food-security stockholding.

prelimsPointers: **Balance of Payments** = **Current Account** (goods, services, transfers) + **Capital Account** (FDI, FII, loans).
India typically runs a **current-account/trade deficit** (crude oil & gold dominate imports).
**WTO (1995)** replaced **GATT (1947)**; HQ **Geneva**.
WTO agreements — **GATT (goods), GATS (services), TRIPS (IP), AoA (agriculture)**.
India defends **public stockholding for food security** (Bali 'Peace Clause').
**Invisibles** (software, remittances) help offset India's trade deficit.
Top exports — **petroleum products, gems, pharma, engineering goods, textiles**.
mainsAngles: Discuss India's balance of payments and its stance in the WTO.

glossary.definition: A record of all economic transactions between residents of a country and the rest of the world.
The World Trade Organization (1995), which frames and enforces global trade rules.
The WTO agreement on Trade-Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights.
